purpose: A received global history of the Cold War, from the collapse of the Grand Alliance at the end of the Second World War through the disintegration of the Soviet Union and its immediate aftermath in 1993. Events are selected as causal anchors for alternate history across superpower diplomacy, the nuclear arms race and its control, proxy wars, ideological and economic competition, domestic repression, dissent and resistance, and the eventual unraveling of the Soviet bloc. It is not an exhaustive chronology of every crisis or campaign.
sourceNote: The chronology synthesizes established scholarly overviews, government historical offices, and reference timelines. It is intended as a sound basis for counterfactual construction rather than original archival research. Dates use the conventional anchor year; ranges and uncertainty are preserved in the display field.

tagLegend.diplomacy: summits, treaties, negotiations, and formal settlements
tagLegend.containment: the US strategy of resisting the expansion of Soviet influence
tagLegend.alliance: military blocs, pacts, and their formation or division

tagLegend.proxy-war: armed conflicts fought through client states and movements

tagLegend.collapse: the disintegration of the Soviet bloc and Union

events.label: Yalta Conference
events.description: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin plan the postwar order, agreeing on occupation zones, free elections in liberated Europe, and Soviet entry into the Pacific war. Rival interpretations of the vague accords soon become a source of distrust.

events.label: Atomic Bombings of Japan
events.description: The United States drops atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, ending the Pacific war and inaugurating the nuclear age with a temporary American monopoly on the decisive new weapon.

events.label: Potsdam Conference
events.description: The victors set terms for occupied Germany and postwar Europe as wartime cooperation gives way to visible friction over reparations, Poland, and the political future of Eastern Europe.

events.label: Kennan's Long Telegram
events.description: US diplomat George Kennan argues that Soviet hostility is rooted in ideology and insecurity and can be met by patient, firm containment, supplying the intellectual basis of American Cold War strategy.

events.label: Churchill's Iron Curtain Speech
events.description: Speaking in Fulton, Missouri, Churchill declares that an iron curtain has descended across Europe, giving public shape to the emerging division of the continent into rival camps.

events.label: Truman Doctrine
events.description: President Truman pledges US support to peoples resisting subjugation, initially aiding Greece and Turkey, and commits the United States to containing communism worldwide.

events.label: Marshall Plan Announced
events.description: The United States offers large-scale aid to rebuild Western European economies, binding recipients to American markets and blunting the appeal of communist parties. The Soviet bloc refuses to participate.

events.label: US National Security Act
events.description: US legislation creates the Central Intelligence Agency, the National Security Council, and a unified defense establishment, building the permanent institutions of American Cold War policy.

events.label: Cominform Established
events.description: Stalin founds the Communist Information Bureau to coordinate European communist parties and enforce a two-camp view of the world, tightening Soviet control over the bloc.

events.label: Czechoslovak Communist Coup
events.description: Communists seize full power in Czechoslovakia, extinguishing the last coalition government in Eastern Europe and hardening Western fears of further Soviet advances.

events.label: Tito–Stalin Split
events.description: Yugoslavia is expelled from the Cominform after Tito resists Soviet dominance, proving that communist states could break with Moscow and opening a path toward non-alignment.

events.label: Berlin Blockade and Airlift
events.description: The Soviet Union blockades West Berlin; a sustained Western airlift supplies the city until the blockade is lifted, the first great confrontation of the Cold War and a symbol of Western resolve.

events.label: NATO Founded
events.description: Twelve Western nations sign the North Atlantic Treaty, committing to collective defense and permanently tying American military power to the security of Western Europe.

events.label: Comecon Established
events.description: The Soviet Union organizes the Council for Mutual Economic Assistance to integrate the economies of its satellites, formalizing a separate Eastern economic bloc.

events.label: Soviet Union Tests an Atomic Bomb
events.description: The first Soviet atomic test ends the American nuclear monopoly years ahead of Western expectations and sets the conditions for a sustained nuclear arms race.

events.label: Two German States Founded
events.description: The Federal Republic of Germany and the German Democratic Republic are established in the western and Soviet occupation zones, entrenching a divided Germany at the center of Europe.

events.label: People's Republic of China Founded
events.description: Communist forces win the Chinese civil war and proclaim the People's Republic while the Nationalists retreat to Taiwan, transforming Asian and global politics and alarming Washington.

events.label: NSC-68 and Rearmament
events.description: A secret US policy paper calls for a massive military buildup to meet the Soviet threat, shifting containment from a mainly economic and political effort toward large-scale rearmament.

events.label: Korean War
events.description: North Korea invades the South; a US-led United Nations force and later Chinese armies turn the divided peninsula into the first major armed conflict of the Cold War, ending in an armistice near the original border.

events.label: McCarthyism and the Red Scare
events.description: Fear of communist subversion drives loyalty investigations, blacklists, and Senator McCarthy's public hearings in the United States, showing how the Cold War reshaped domestic politics and civil liberties.

events.label: Rosenberg Atomic Espionage Case
events.description: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg are convicted and executed for passing atomic secrets to the Soviet Union, dramatizing wartime nuclear espionage and the intensity of American anticommunist anxiety.

events.label: United States Tests a Hydrogen Bomb
events.description: The first American thermonuclear test yields explosive power far beyond fission weapons, escalating the arms race toward city-destroying bombs and provoking a Soviet counterpart within a year.

events.label: Death of Stalin
events.description: Stalin's death opens a succession struggle in the Soviet Union and a cautious thaw, making possible the Korean armistice and the first tentative easing of the harshest repression.

events.label: East German Uprising
events.description: Workers' protests in East Germany spread into a broad revolt that Soviet tanks suppress, the first of several risings that revealed the fragility of Soviet control over its satellites.

events.label: Dien Bien Phu and the Geneva Accords
events.description: French defeat in Indochina and the Geneva settlement partition Vietnam pending elections, ending French empire in the region and drawing the United States toward a widening commitment in Southeast Asia.

events.label: Warsaw Pact Formed
events.description: In response to West German rearmament and NATO membership, the Soviet Union and its satellites form a rival military alliance, formalizing the bloc structure of Cold War Europe.

events.label: Bandung Conference
events.description: Newly independent Asian and African states meet at Bandung to assert solidarity and independence from both blocs, seeding the Non-Aligned Movement and a distinct third-world politics.

events.label: Khrushchev's Secret Speech
events.description: Khrushchev denounces Stalin's crimes and cult of personality before the Party Congress, launching de-Stalinization and unsettling communist parties and satellites across the bloc.

events.label: Hungarian Revolution
events.description: A national uprising installs a reform government that declares neutrality and withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact; Soviet forces crush it, setting the limits of permissible change in the bloc.

events.label: Suez Crisis
events.description: Britain, France, and Israel attack Egypt over the nationalized Suez Canal but withdraw under US and Soviet pressure, exposing the decline of European empires and the primacy of the superpowers.

events.label: Sputnik Launched
events.description: The Soviet Union orbits the first artificial satellite, alarming the West about a possible missile gap and igniting a space race that fused prestige, science, and intercontinental rocketry.

events.label: Cuban Revolution
events.description: Fidel Castro's forces overthrow the Cuban government and move toward the Soviet camp, placing a communist ally ninety miles from Florida and reshaping US policy in the Western Hemisphere.

events.label: U-2 Incident
events.description: The Soviet Union shoots down an American U-2 spy plane and captures its pilot, wrecking a planned Paris summit and hardening relations after a brief period of thaw.

events.label: Sino-Soviet Split
events.description: Ideological and strategic disputes rupture the alliance between Moscow and Beijing, fracturing the communist world into rival centers and reshaping the global balance for decades.

events.label: Bay of Pigs Invasion
events.description: A CIA-backed invasion by Cuban exiles fails disastrously, humiliating the United States, entrenching Castro, and pushing Cuba further into Soviet protection.

events.label: First Human Spaceflight
events.description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in orbit, a propaganda triumph that spurs the United States to commit to landing a man on the Moon.

events.label: Berlin Wall Built
events.description: East Germany seals off West Berlin with a wall to stop the hemorrhage of refugees, stabilizing the German front of the Cold War while creating its most potent symbol of division.

events.label: Cuban Missile Crisis
events.description: The discovery of Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba brings the superpowers to the brink of nuclear war; a negotiated withdrawal, paired with a secret US pledge on missiles in Turkey, ends the closest call of the Cold War.

events.label: Partial Test Ban Treaty
events.description: The United States, Soviet Union, and Britain ban atmospheric, underwater, and space nuclear tests, the first major arms-control accord and an early product of post-crisis caution.

events.label: Gulf of Tonkin and US Escalation
events.description: Reported clashes off Vietnam prompt a US congressional resolution authorizing wider military action, opening the way to full American intervention in the Vietnam War.

events.label: China Tests an Atomic Bomb
events.description: The People's Republic of China detonates its first nuclear device, joining the nuclear club, complicating superpower calculations, and deepening the Sino-Soviet rift.

events.label: Khrushchev Ousted
events.description: Soviet leaders remove Khrushchev and install Brezhnev, ending the reformist thaw and beginning a long era of conservative stability, military buildup, and bureaucratic stagnation.

events.label: Americanization of the Vietnam War
events.description: The United States commits large ground forces and a sustained bombing campaign to defend South Vietnam, turning a proxy conflict into a major war that would strain American society and finances.

events.label: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
events.description: A landmark treaty commits signatories to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and to pursue disarmament, creating the central legal framework for limiting the nuclear club.

events.label: Prague Spring Crushed
events.description: Warsaw Pact forces invade Czechoslovakia to end its reform movement; the Brezhnev Doctrine asserts Moscow's right to intervene against liberalization, disillusioning communists worldwide.

events.label: Tet Offensive
events.description: A massive coordinated assault across South Vietnam, though militarily costly to its attackers, shatters American confidence in a near victory and turns US public opinion against the war.

events.label: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
events.description: American astronauts land on the Moon, giving the United States a decisive symbolic victory in the space race and a demonstration of technological and organizational power.

events.label: Sino-Soviet Border Clashes
events.description: Armed clashes along the Ussuri River bring China and the Soviet Union close to war, pushing Beijing toward an eventual opening with the United States.

events.label: Nixon Visits China
events.description: President Nixon's visit to Beijing begins a rapprochement between the United States and the People's Republic, creating a triangular diplomacy that pressures Moscow and reorders the Cold War.

events.label: SALT I and ABM Treaty
events.description: US and Soviet leaders sign the first Strategic Arms Limitation accords and a treaty restricting missile defenses, institutionalizing détente and mutual nuclear vulnerability.

events.label: Paris Peace Accords
events.description: An agreement ends direct US military involvement in Vietnam and withdraws American forces, leaving the divided country's fate to be decided by continued fighting.

events.label: Yom Kippur War and Oil Crisis
events.description: An Arab-Israeli war draws in superpower clients and triggers an Arab oil embargo, straining détente and revealing the economic vulnerability of the industrialized West.

events.label: Fall of Saigon
events.description: North Vietnamese forces capture Saigon and reunify Vietnam under communist rule, a defeat that shook American confidence and shaped a generation's view of foreign intervention.

events.label: Helsinki Accords
events.description: European and North American states accept existing borders and pledge to respect human rights; the rights provisions unexpectedly empower dissident movements across the Eastern bloc.

events.label: Angolan Civil War Internationalized
events.description: The end of Portuguese empire in Angola opens a civil war in which Soviet and Cuban support faces Western-backed rivals, extending superpower rivalry into post-colonial Africa.

events.label: SALT II Signed
events.description: The United States and Soviet Union sign a second strategic arms accord, but rising tensions prevent US ratification, marking the fraying of détente.

events.label: NATO Dual-Track Decision
events.description: NATO agrees to deploy new intermediate-range missiles in Western Europe while offering arms-control talks, provoking a Soviet counter-buildup and a wave of Western peace protests.

events.label: Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan
events.description: Soviet forces intervene to prop up a communist government in Afghanistan, ending détente, prompting Western sanctions and boycotts, and beginning a long, draining guerrilla war.

events.label: Solidarity Movement in Poland
events.description: Strikes at the Gdansk shipyard produce Solidarity, the first independent mass trade union in the Soviet bloc, a durable challenge to communist authority rooted in workers and the Church.

events.label: Martial Law in Poland
events.description: Poland's government imposes martial law and bans Solidarity to forestall Soviet intervention, driving the opposition underground while leaving communist legitimacy fatally weakened.

events.label: Reagan's SDI and Evil Empire Speech
events.description: President Reagan denounces the Soviet Union as an evil empire and proposes a space-based missile defense, intensifying rhetoric and pressuring Soviet resources at a moment of economic weakness.

events.label: Able Archer War Scare
events.description: A NATO command exercise, misread by a fearful Soviet leadership as possible cover for a first strike, brings the superpowers to an underappreciated moment of nuclear danger.

events.label: Gorbachev Becomes Soviet Leader
events.description: Mikhail Gorbachev takes power determined to revive a stagnant system, launching glasnost and perestroika and seeking to relax tensions in order to reform at home.

events.label: Chernobyl Disaster
events.description: The explosion at a Soviet nuclear plant spreads radiation across Europe; the initial cover-up and eventual disclosure test glasnost and expose the failures of the Soviet system.

events.label: Reykjavik Summit
events.description: Reagan and Gorbachev nearly agree to abolish nuclear weapons before deadlocking over missile defense, a startling near-breakthrough that set the stage for real arms reductions.

events.label: INF Treaty
events.description: The United States and Soviet Union agree to eliminate an entire class of intermediate-range nuclear missiles, the first treaty to abolish rather than merely limit a category of weapons.

events.label: Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan
events.description: The Soviet Union completes its withdrawal from Afghanistan after a costly decade of war, signaling the retreat of Soviet power and emboldening reform across the bloc.

events.label: Revolutions of 1989
events.description: Semi-free elections in Poland, an opened Hungarian border, and mass protests topple communist governments across Eastern Europe as Moscow declines to intervene, unraveling the bloc within months.

events.label: Fall of the Berlin Wall
events.description: East Germany opens its borders and crowds breach the Berlin Wall, the defining image of the Cold War's end and a prelude to German reunification.

events.label: Malta Summit
events.description: Meeting off Malta, Bush and Gorbachev declare an end to superpower hostility, effectively announcing that the Cold War is over even as the Soviet bloc continues to dissolve.

events.label: German Reunification
events.description: East and West Germany unite within NATO after negotiated Soviet consent, ending the central territorial division of the Cold War in Europe.

events.label: Warsaw Pact Dissolved
events.description: The Eastern military alliance is formally disbanded as its members turn westward, dismantling the institutional framework of the Soviet bloc.

events.label: START I Signed
events.description: The United States and Soviet Union agree to substantial reductions in strategic nuclear arsenals, converting the easing of tensions into deep, verifiable cuts.

events.label: August Coup in Moscow
events.description: Hardliners briefly seize power to halt reform and preserve the Union; popular resistance in Moscow defeats them, fatally discrediting the Communist Party and accelerating the Union's breakup.

events.label: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
events.description: The Soviet Union is formally dissolved into fifteen independent states and Gorbachev resigns, ending both the USSR and the Cold War order it had anchored.

events.label: Russian Economic Shock Therapy
events.description: Post-Soviet Russia frees prices and begins rapid privatization, producing steep inflation, collapsing output, and social dislocation that shaped the troubled birth of the new state.

events.label: START II Signed
events.description: The United States and Russia agree to further deep cuts in strategic nuclear weapons, extending Cold War arms control into the post-Soviet era.

events.label: Russian Constitutional Crisis
events.description: A violent standoff between President Yeltsin and the parliament ends with tanks shelling the legislature, revealing the instability of Russia's post-Soviet order in the immediate aftermath of the Cold War.
